outcome: A February 2025 arXiv preprint by Rui Li, Zida Xiao and Huaiqing Zuo extends the Nakai conjecture to local domains and verifies it for isolated hypersurface singularities of modality ≤ 2, settling a restricted case of the conjecture (the general conjecture, and even the local-domain extension in general, remains open).
summary: The frozen Wikipedia bullet states the Nakai conjecture (1961): if the ring of differential operators of a complex algebraic variety is generated by degree-one derivations, the variety is smooth. The only development found in the window (26 Jan 2024–present) is arXiv:2502.04672, 'The Nakai Conjecture for isolated hypersurface singularities of modality ≤ 2' by Rui Li, Zida Xiao and Huaiqing Zuo, posted 7 February 2025 (single version, no later revisions). The paper explicitly frames itself as extending the conjecture to local domains and then verifying that extension for a specific, restricted class of singularities (isolated hypersurface singularities of modality ≤ 2), stating this 'extends the existing works.' This is a genuine case of the problem under §3.1: it restricts the class of algebras/varieties considered (to a specific singularity type and modality bound) rather than changing the question being asked, so settling it removes territory from the open problem. It does not resolve the conjecture in general — the Wikipedia article and all sources checked confirm the conjecture (equivalently implying the Zariski–Lipman conjecture) remains open outside a handful of known cases (algebraic curves, Stanley–Reisner rings, normal toric varieties). I read the arXiv abstract page directly (submission date, version history, MSC classes) and attempted to read the full PDF text; the PDF's text layer did not extract cleanly via the fetch tool, but the abstract, title, and all secondary discussion (a literature-review summary site, arXiv listing pages) are consistent and contain no mention of AI, machine learning, automated theorem proving, or computer algebra methods — this is a conventional human-authored proof in singularity theory. There is no evidence the paper has been digested by outside experts (no blog coverage, no citing survey found) or accepted to a journal of record as of this search, so it is classified `partial` rather than `resolved`: a genuine sub-case has been settled, using a status separate from the resolved/claimed distinction (which concerns the general conjecture, not this restricted result) — the case itself is a fully worked, verifiable mathematical proof in a preprint, not a machine-generated or machine-checked claim awaiting expert review, so it earns `partial` with `resolution_direction: confirmed` (the conjecture holds in the case verified) rather than being downgraded for lack of digestion. I also searched broadly for any other 2024–2026 work on Nakai/Zariski–Lipman and found only unrelated results: a GitHub tracking issue (google-deepmind/formal-conjectures#1822) requesting a Lean formalization of the (distinct, though related) Zariski–Lipman conjecture, which remains open/unformalized and does not mention Nakai at all, so it is out of scope and not counted.
competing_reading: One could argue the paper's 'extension to local domains' changes the object of study (global finite-type algebras over a field vs. local domains) enough to make this a related/variant problem rather than a case of the stated conjecture, in which case the correct status would be `open` with `no_change_found: true` and this preprint noted only as beside the point. I judge it as a case rather than a variant because the authors present the local-domain extension explicitly as a natural strengthening/instance of the same conjecture (same hypothesis about the ring of differential operators being generated by first-order derivations, same conclusion of regularity/smoothness) applied to a narrower, well-defined class of rings, and prior literature on Nakai's conjecture routinely treats the local (singularity-theoretic) formulation as the natural setting for verifying cases — Wikipedia's own 'known to be true for algebraic curves' case is itself a local/specific-class result of exactly this kind.
what_would_settle_it: Reading the full paper text (not just the abstract) to confirm the precise logical relationship between the 'extended to local domains' statement and the original finite-type-algebra statement, and checking whether any published survey or expert commentary treats this modality-≤2 result as a bona fide case of the classical Nakai conjecture or flags it as a distinct local variant.

corrections.why: other: kept as partial. The competing_reading argues the local-domain extension may be a variant, but the paper verifies a strengthened form of the same statement (same hypothesis, same regularity conclusion) on a restricted class of singularities, which is a case of the bullet. The record did not confirm this from the full text, so there is residual doubt.

events.what: Li, Xiao and Zuo extend the Nakai conjecture to local domains and verify it for isolated hypersurface singularities of modality ≤ 2

judgement.doubts: The case/variant call is the only real question. The local-domain formulation has the same hypothesis and conclusion and is a strengthening, so its truth for the local rings of modality ≤ 2 isolated hypersurface singularities should cover varieties whose singular points are all of that type; that makes it a restriction (case), not a changed question. But the researcher never read the full text, so the exact implication back to the finite-type statement was not confirmed. The absence of AI is inferred from the abstract and secondary summaries only. The Zariski–Lipman formal-conjectures issue is correctly excluded.
